Personal project, developed during the PhD | 2025 - present

## Overview

FBGA - Forward-Backward Generic Acceleration constraints - computes the
maximum-performance velocity profile along a path given a complex g-g-v
constraint envelope: the combined longitudinal/lateral acceleration limits a
vehicle can actually sustain, which change with speed and aren't a simple
circle or ellipse. Given a path's curvature profile and that envelope, the
forward-backward algorithm finds the fastest velocity profile that never
asks the vehicle for more grip than it has, running fast enough for
real-time use rather than offline-only optimization. Existing
forward-backward planners get their speed by assuming a simple (typically
convex) shape for the g-g-v envelope so they can pre-compute the apexes to
build the profile around; FBGA instead locates the switching points
adaptively while it propagates the solution, so it needs no assumption at
all about the envelope's shape - it treats it as a black box that can be
evaluated point by point, whether it comes from a formula, a lookup table,
or a high-fidelity vehicle model.

## Accuracy and speed

Validated against an indirect optimal control solver (Pins) across five
racetracks and two vehicle classes (race car, motorcycle), the 2D solver
matches lap times to within roughly 0.1-0.4%, while running up to three
orders of magnitude faster - down to fractions of a millisecond per query,
well within budget for online, onboard planning. Within a 300 m receding
horizon representative of a moving-horizon planner, it solves in a
fraction of a millisecond regardless of mesh size, against several
milliseconds for the OCP.

## From 2D to 3D

The library started as a 2D solver - curvature-only path, single g-g
envelope - published as [*Real-Time Velocity Profile Optimization for
Time-Optimal Maneuvering With Generic Acceleration
Constraints*](https://doi.org/10.1109/LRA.2025.3643297) (IEEE Robotics and
Automation Letters, 2025). It has since grown a 3D solver, generic over
the vehicle's g-g-v model, that accounts for banked and pitched paths
(Suzuka, Laguna Seca, Yas Marina), load transfer, spatially variable grip,
and yellow-flag deceleration limits - published as [*Beyond the Apex:
Online Minimum-Time Velocity Planning on Three-Dimensional Paths With
Variable Friction*](https://doi.org/10.1109/LRA.2026.3707351) (IEEE
Robotics and Automation Letters, 2026).
Unlike prior 3D forward-backward methods, it drops the assumption that a
maneuver's apex sits at the geometric corner apex, computing it adaptively
instead - within 0.2-0.3% of an OCP baseline and up to 44x faster than the
closest prior forward-backward method, while eliminating the g-g-v
violations (up to several percent) that apex precomputation causes on
tracks with pronounced 3D geometry. It also natively handles non-convex
envelopes, such as a motorcycle's no-wheeling/no-stoppie limits, which the
super-elliptical formulation used by prior 3D methods cannot represent.
The 3D solver was originally developed as its own repository,
[FBGA_3D](https://github.com/mattiapzz/FBGA_3D), and is now ported into
FBGA itself as an opt-in module.

## Related publications

- [*Real-Time Velocity Profile Optimization for Time-Optimal Maneuvering
  With Generic Acceleration Constraints*](https://doi.org/10.1109/LRA.2025.3643297),
  IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 2025 - the original 2D FBGA paper.
- [*Beyond the Apex: Online Minimum-Time Velocity Planning on
  Three-Dimensional Paths With Variable
  Friction*](https://doi.org/10.1109/LRA.2026.3707351), IEEE Robotics and
  Automation Letters, 2026 - the 3D extension.

Two more papers building on FBGA are set to appear in their conference
proceedings:

- *Fast GGV-Compliant Sampling-Based Planning for Vehicles*, presented at
  AVEC 2026 (Tsukuba, Japan) - a JSAE Best Paper Award finalist. FBGA is
  used here as the trajectory-evaluation module inside a sampling-based
  planner running on a scaled autonomous racing vehicle.

- [*Trajectory Planning and Control near the Limits: an Open Experimental
  Benchmark on the RoboRacer Platform*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19881),
  IEEE ITSC 2026 (Naples) - an open benchmark where FBGA runs as the
  real-time velocity re-planner on the same scaled platform, in a
  different architectural role from the AVEC application.

## Where it runs

Used in the TUM Autonomous Vehicle Systems Laboratory's Indy Autonomous
Challenge and Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League entries, where it was
benchmarked directly against the velocity planner the team actually races
with - not an academic baseline.

## Adoption

Beyond my own use, FBGA has drawn interest from outside its original
domain, all through unsolicited contact:

- A TUM group working on uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) inquired about
  applying it to thrust/attitude envelopes, which are similarly
  non-convex and state-dependent.
- A conversation with an Italian industrial vehicle manufacturer at IEEE
  ICRA 2026 about a possible collaboration, still exploratory.
- An ongoing collaboration with Philipp Braun's group (CIICADA Lab,
  Australian National University) has a joint paper in preparation.

The library is also distributed as an installable
[Python package](https://pypi.org/project/fbga-py/), which lowers the bar
for anyone to try it without going through a prior agreement.

## Status

Public C++ library, maintained solely by me, hosted under the DRIVEWISE
organization. 2025 - present.
